scope: Arbitrary-multiplicity products and homogeneous sums of primitive growing beta Casoratians against any Item265 de-overlapped target divisor

claims.label: PROVED
claims.claim: For every Q|q_n and every finite weighted product A=product P_h(n)^w_h, gcd(Q,A) divides product gcd(Q,P_h(n))^w_h; the associated scalar-Casoratian product has the same gcd with Q.
claims.evidence: report Section 2, exact primewise truncated valuation identities
claims.scope_limit: weights and support may depend on n, but gaps satisfy h>=2 and Q is declared explicitly

claims.label: PROVED
claims.claim: Captured logarithmic capacity per residual height is at most the largest primitive overlap efficiency log gcd(Q,P_h(n))/log P_h(n).
claims.evidence: report equations (2.5) and the weighted-average argument
claims.scope_limit: this is necessary, not sufficient, because target exponents can saturate under repetition

claims.label: PROVED
claims.claim: An O(n)-height portfolio has K<=L=O(n/log n); positive linear captured capacity forces a gap O(n/log n) with primitive overlap occupying a fixed positive fraction of log P_h(n).
claims.scope_limit: no actual-family theorem currently produces or excludes such a high-efficiency return

claims.label: PROVED
claims.claim: For G_t=gcd(Q,P_h(n)^t), the layer quotients G_t/G_(t-1) form a divisibility-decreasing chain.
claims.evidence: report equation (3.1), exact primewise layer exponent
claims.scope_limit: powering creates no new prime support and has diminishing return, but can scale existing overlap

claims.label: PROVED_SCOPED_NO_GO
claims.claim: With unrestricted factor count, the least canonical anti-period gap cost for certified p-depth s is s(p-1), so every O(n)-height canonical portfolio has only O(n/log n)=o(n) certified logarithmic capacity, even across multiple assigned primes.
claims.scope_limit: accidental target divisibility of canonical continuants is noncanonical high-efficiency overlap and is not ruled out

claims.label: PROVED_RECOGNITION
claims.claim: The exact remaining product input is the weighted return-cover optimization Y_Q(n;B); a positive-linear theorem at B=O(n/log n), or full target divisibility, would be admissible.
claims.scope_limit: neither the positive-linear lower bound nor full cover is proved for actual moving rows

claims.label: PROVED_SUM_DICHOTOMY
claims.claim: A homogeneous scalar-Casoratian sum has the same target gcd as its primitive residual sum; a unique least p-adic term gives exactly that minimum, while only tied minima can create a sum-only cancellation factor.
claims.scope_limit: nonhomogeneous sums and coefficients depending on target factorization are not admitted by this recognition

claims.label: PROVED_DEOVERLAP
claims.claim: Every product and sum statement applies to any target Q dividing q_n/gcd(q_n,D_m), so the Item265 clearing reservoir is removed before capacity is measured.
claims.scope_limit: a booked gain would still require an actual-family mass theorem and the stated transverse matching correlation

claims.label: EXACT_FINITE_ONLY
claims.claim: The deterministic checker replays product capture, overlap majorization, scalar/residual equality, diminishing layers, the unrestricted canonical optimizer, and homogeneous-sum cancellation on bounded exact ranges.
claims.scope_limit: the tied-cancellation witness is algebraic illustration only; no exceptional-singleton census or asymptotic extrapolation is performed

claims.label: OPEN_NOT_PROVED
claims.claim: No actual high-efficiency return mass, weighted cover, prime-independent cancellation divisibility, uniform prime-power height, or little-oh squarefull theorem is obtained.
claims.scope_limit: Item282 is not a general no-go for sums or genuinely new global auxiliaries

claims.label: PROVED_BOOKING_DECISION
claims.claim: The positive-linear capacity admission test fails; no new Route-1 rate or beta capacity reduction is booked.
claims.scope_limit: the Item265 high-singleton ceiling and two-copy normalization remain unchanged
